nodes.summary: Let $(p, q, e, d)$ be an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$, and let $d_p, d_q \ge 1$ be natural numbers with $d_p \equiv d \pmod{p - 1}$ and $d_q \equiv d \pmod{q - 1}$. Then for every $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, RSA-CRT decryption of $c$ with the exponents $d_p$ and $d_q$ equals the RSA decryption $c^d$.
nodes.title: RSA-CRT decryption is correct

nodes.summary: Let $(p, q, e, d)$ be an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ in which both primes are odd, that is $p > 2$ and $q > 2$. Then for every $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, RSA-CRT decryption of $c$ with the exponents $d_p = d \bmod (p - 1)$ and $d_q = d \bmod (q - 1)$ equals the RSA decryption $c^d$.
nodes.title: RSA-CRT decryption with the standard exponents

nodes.summary: Let $(p, q, e, d)$ be an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$. For natural numbers $d_p$, $d_q$ and $c \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, let $c_p$ and $c_q$ be the images of $c$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$. RSA-CRT decryption of $c$ with the exponents $d_p$ and $d_q$ is the element of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ that corresponds to the pair $(c_p^{d_p}, c_q^{d_q})$ under the Chinese remainder…
nodes.title: RSA-CRT decryption

nodes.summary: For an RSA key with distinct primes $p$, $q$ and modulus $n = pq$, this is the ring isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ of the Chinese remainder theorem, sending $x$ to $(x \bmod p, x \bmod q)$.
nodes.title: Chinese remainder isomorphism for an RSA modulus

nodes.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and exponents $e$, $d$, every natural number $m < n$ satisfies $(m^e \bmod n)^d \bmod n = m$.
nodes.title: Correctness of textbook RSA on natural numbers

nodes.summary: Decryption inverts encryption on every message, including messages that are not coprime to `n`.
nodes.title: Correctness of textbook RSA

nodes.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and private exponent $d$, decryption is the map $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ given by $c \mapsto c^d$.
nodes.title: RSA decryption

nodes.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and public exponent $e$, the encryption map $m \mapsto m^e$ is a bijection from $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ to itself.
nodes.title: RSA encryption is a bijection

nodes.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n = pq$ and public exponent $e$, encryption is the map $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ given by $m \mapsto m^e$.
nodes.title: RSA encryption

nodes.summary: A textbook RSA key consists of distinct primes $p$ and $q$ and natural numbers $e$ (the public exponent) and $d$ (the private exponent) such that $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{p - 1}$ and $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{q - 1}$.
nodes.title: RSA key

nodes.summary: The modulus of an RSA key with primes $p$ and $q$ is $n = pq$.
nodes.title: RSA modulus

nodes.summary: Given distinct primes $p$ and $q$ and natural numbers $e$ and $d$ with $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{\varphi(pq)}$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function, this is the RSA key with primes $p$ and $q$, public exponent $e$ and private exponent $d$. Its conditions $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{p - 1}$ and $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{q - 1}$ hold because $\varphi(pq) = (p - 1)(q - 1)$.
nodes.title: RSA key from the totient condition

nodes.summary: Let $p$, $e$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $p > 2$ and $ed \equiv 1 \pmod{p - 1}$. Then $d \bmod (p - 1) \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Positivity of the reduced RSA exponent

nodes.summary: For an RSA key with modulus $n$ and exponents $e$ and $d$, every $x \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ satisfies $x^{ed} = x$.
nodes.title: RSA exponent identity

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $a, b \ge 1$ and $a \equiv b \pmod{p - 1}$. Then $x^a = x^b$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Fermat's little theorem for congruent exponents

nodes.summary: Let an RSA key have primes $p$ and $q$ and modulus $n$, let $k$ be a natural number and $x \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, and let $(x_p, x_q) \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ be the image of $x$ under the Chinese remainder isomorphism. If $x_p^k = x_p$ and $x_q^k = x_q$, then $x^k = x$.
nodes.title: Checking a power identity through the Chinese remainder theorem

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $k \ge 1$ be a natural number with $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p - 1}$. Then $x^k = x$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Fermat's little theorem with exponents congruent to one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
